question: Should Gitcrawl adopt this exact immutable snapshot, staged cutover, fail-closed compatibility, and operator-owned private-content retention contract as the supported cloud publication model?
rationale: The implementation appears technically coherent, but the permanent cross-service upgrade and data-lifecycle contract requires explicit maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve after exact-head proof
options.body: Accept the model after fresh publication, stage-only, completed staged resume, reader-query, cutover, mismatch-rejection, sanitization, and lifecycle evidence from the intended service versions.

options.title: Hold for coordinated deployment
options.body: Keep the draft open until crawl-remote provenance support and bounded lifecycle controls are deployed and upgrade-tested as one compatible service set.

options.title: Narrow the publication model
options.body: Defer staged activation or immutable bundle publication if maintainers do not want the coordinated upgrade and retention obligations.

recommendation.title: Approve after exact-head proof
recommendation.body: Accept the model after fresh publication, stage-only, completed staged resume, reader-query, cutover, mismatch-rejection, sanitization, and lifecycle evidence from the intended service versions.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository and branch history make this person the clearest available owner to coordinate the cross-service decision.
